children: Argentina's economy grew 2.0% in the second quarter from a year earlier, government statistics agency INDEC said on Thursday, beating analyst expectations as mining, agriculture and exports helped support economic activity.
Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 1.6% for the April-to-June period.

The year-on-year increase was driven mainly by the fishing sector, which expanded 45% from a year earlier, while mining and quarrying rose 16% and agriculture, livestock, hunting and forestry increased 7%, according to the report.
Exports of goods and services climbed 14% from a year earlier, while imports fell 9%.
Manufacturing posted one of the sharpest declines among major sectors, contracting 2% from a year earlier.
In seasonally adjusted terms, GDP fell 0.6% from the first quarter, the first quarterly contraction after a 0.7% increase in the January-March period.

The data offer one of the broadest snapshots of economic activity under libertarian President Javier Milei's reform program. Argentina has seen inflation cool sharply from triple-digit levels recorded early in Milei's administration, while the government has pursued fiscal austerity measures aimed at eliminating chronic budget deficits.
